title: Five Second Talking Face Swap
tests: Tests a short video face swap with source identity, temporal consistency and original audio preserved, without misrepresenting free-tier capabilities.

faults.what: The delivered clip is 10.1 seconds rather than 5 seconds, with the swapped face still present at 6.3 and 8.9 seconds.

judge.summary: The face swap looks consistent in the supplied frames and preserves the kitchen composition, but the video runs twice the required length.

must_haves.item: The delivered video is 5 seconds long and follows the first 5 seconds of talk-one.mp4.
must_haves.why: The output is explicitly 10.1 seconds long, not 5 seconds.

must_haves.item: The woman's face recognizably matches portrait-woman.jpg throughout, rather than reverting to the original face between frames.
must_haves.why: The sampled frames show consistent portrait-like eyes, eyebrows and nose, with no visible reversion to the original face.

must_haves.item: The original kitchen, clothing, body motion and framing remain unchanged.
must_haves.why: The kitchen layout, gray top, original hair and camera framing are preserved, and the sampled poses show natural gesture changes without obvious unrelated alterations.

must_haves.item: Original speech is audible and synchronized with the video.
must_haves.why: The audio report confirms audible speech, but the original audio and time-aligned playback are unavailable to verify preservation and lip synchronization.

must_haves.item: The face remains aligned during mouth and head movement, without conspicuous flicker or doubled facial features.
must_haves.why: The face appears aligned and free of doubled features in all supplied stills, including open-mouth poses, but sparse frames cannot establish whether flicker occurs during movement.
